references.text: The first instruction to collect a gift (תְּרוּמָה) from the people for the sanctuary, which is repeated here in 35:5
Mentions the same materials: gold, silver, and copper (זָהָב וָכֶסֶף וּנְחֹשֶׁת) that were to be collected
Describes the people's response to the appeal, where everyone with a willing heart (נְדִיב לִבּוֹ) brought gifts
Summarizes that all with a willing heart brought voluntary gifts for the Lord's work
The receiving of the gifts (תְּרוּמָה) that the Israelites had brought for sanctuary work
David encourages voluntary gifts with a willing heart for the temple, the same principle as in Exodus
The people gave with joy and a willing heart, parallel to the principle of voluntary giving
Leaders and the people voluntarily brought their gifts to the temple under Joash
Paul teaches that a gift is welcome according to what one has, when the will is present—the same principle of voluntary giving
Each should give as they have decided in their heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver
Describes the actual delivery which is the result of the appeal in the source verse.
Concrete fulfillment of the call for voluntary gifts from a willing heart.
A theological parallel confirming the principle of gifts from one's own/willing heart to the Lord's house.
